claims.text: Superconducting transition temperature in high-entropy alloys is primarily governed by local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions modulate electron–phonon coupling strength.
The proposed as-cast, compositionally complex HEA exhibits superconductivity.
Controlled annealing can reduce local lattice distortions without significantly changing overall composition.
Local lattice distortions alter the phonon spectrum.
Changes in the phonon spectrum caused by lattice distortions affect the electron–phonon coupling constant.
Reducing lattice distortions enhances the uniformity of the electron–phonon interaction.
Reducing lattice distortions increases the strength of the electron–phonon interaction.
A stronger and more uniform electron–phonon interaction increases the superconducting transition temperature.
Compositional disorder produces a high degree of local lattice distortion.
Local lattice distortions broaden phonon modes and introduce scattering.
Phonon-mode broadening and scattering caused by local distortions weaken electron–phonon coupling.
Annealed HEA samples with suppressed local distortions will have a higher superconducting transition temperature than as-cast samples.
Annealed HEA samples with suppressed local distortions will have a more uniform superconducting transition than as-cast samples.
Rapid solidification causes the as-cast baseline to have relatively high local lattice distortion.
The proposed mechanism is expected to be significant in non-magnetic, electron–phonon-mediated superconductors.
Magnetic impurities or excessive alloy scattering can obscure the proposed lattice-distortion mechanism.
Annealing-induced changes in phase composition can confound the proposed comparison.
XRD and TEM measurements can be used to assess lattice-distortion differences between the sample groups.
Failure of annealed samples to show a higher or more homogeneous transition temperature despite a statistically significant reduction in distortion would falsify the proposed hypothesis.
